questions.question: The commit and push gates miss `git -C <path> commit|push`, and since #1175 that silently strands held decision records. How do we handle it?

options.label: File BK item + fix now (Recommended)
options.description: New backlog item, failing hook test first, fix on a fresh branch from master, one PR. Closes the hole before more cloud sessions lose held dialogs.

options.label: File BK item only
options.description: Record the diagnosis and evidence in a backlog item and dossier; no code now. Sessions keep bypassing both gates until someone picks it up.

options.label: Fold into PR #1178
options.description: The other session's open BK-485 PR already edits settings.json. Fewer PRs, but it widens an unrelated tooling PR and that session would have to own it.

questions.question: If we fix it, how should the gates catch `git -C` forms?

options.label: Drop `if:`, rely on command_mentions (Recommended)
options.description: gate-commit/gate-push run on every Bash call and filter themselves via command-check.sh, which already matches `git -C "$PWD" commit`. Robust to any flag order; costs one bash+jq spawn per Bash call.

options.label: Add `git -C * commit*` if-patterns
options.description: Extra hook entries with a mid-pattern wildcard. Cheap, but still misses `git -c x commit`, `cd x && git commit` etc., and depends on the harness's wildcard semantics.

options.label: Both, plus honour -C path in gate
options.description: Drop `if:` and also make the gate read the branch from the `-C` directory, not the hook's cwd, so worktree commits are judged on the right branch. Most correct, largest diff.
